message.content: In lions, one of the most noticeable dominant genetic traits is the presence of a mane in adult males. The gene responsible for mane development is expressed dominantly, meaning that if a male lion inherits the allele for mane growth from either parent, it will typically develop a mane as it matures. This trait is strongly influenced by testosterone levels, but the underlying genetic predisposition for mane growth follows a dominant inheritance pattern.
